intended_object: An auxiliary construction for the Mackey double-coset formula in continuous cohomology. Given open subgroups H and K, and for each double coset HxK a right transversal T_x of the stabilizer K ∩ x⁻¹Hx in K, it bundles the set {x·t : x a chosen double-coset representative, t ∈ T_x} as a right transversal of H in G. I read this from the docstring and from how it is used in `transferCrossed_mackey_apply`.
explanation:
This is the bookkeeping step in the proof of the Mackey formula: it assembles chosen representatives into a transversal so that the transfer can later be rewritten as a sum over double cosets. Mathematically it is just a lemma with chosen data, namely the decomposition G = ⊔_x HxK with HxK = ⊔_{t∈T_x} H·x·t. It is not a standard object one would expect Mathlib to define.

The body carries the set `Set.range (mackeyAssembledRepresentative H K T)` together with a proof of `IsComplement H S` (existence and uniqueness of the factorisation g = h·s), and that is mathematically correct. The definition is stated for `OpenSubgroup`s, although the group theory would work for any subgroups. The open-subgroup setting is the one this library needs: the stabilizer is taken as an open subgroup of K so that the transfer stays continuous.

Since this is a proof device and not a standalone mathematical notion, the verdict is `not_a_mathematical_object`. As a construction it is correct.
